name: The Granddaughter of Smoke
description: Shot on salvaged flat-screen rigs over fourteen months in the the Gray Zone districts of what was once Waukegan, this film follows Paz Oduya-Lindqvist, a twelve-year-old girl who tends a rooftop garden as her neighborhood is condemned by an infrastructure authority. Director Yemisi Boateng-Harari refused BCI capture, insisting the distance of the flat image was thematically necessary — the viewer must remain a witness, not a participant. Distributed physically on data chips before a mesh upload made it globally accessible.
cultural_impact: Became a foundational text for the Flat-Screen Resistance aesthetic movement, which argues that neural-feed immersion is a tool of corporate empathy manipulation.
story_hooks: The rooftop garden location is real and still exists; someone has been leaving data chips with the film hidden among the planters for years.
Axiom Civic Solutions is now offering Yemisi Boateng-Harari a licensed deal to remake the film as a neural-feed 'urban renewal' piece — and she is considering it.
Paz, the child actor, is now an adult activist whose identity has been scrubbed from licensed databases.
